clue.text: You may get a lift following introduction to classical composer

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of classical

blocks.clueFragment: You may get a lift following
blocks.note: 'hop in' is what a driver says when offering you a lift

explanation.surface: A tip that a dose of classical music will cheer you up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lift' looks like a mood boost; it is a ride in a car, and 'following' means the words come after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was a Polish Romantic pianist-composer, an example of a composer of classical music.

clue.text: Old sexy nurses giving hilarious performance

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one word cradles the other inside it

blocks.note: hot means sexy, attractive
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A saucy old nurse puts on a riotously funny show.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside HOT to make HOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoot is informal for something or someone very funny, such as an uproarious show.

clue.text: How to break Cappuccino-only loyalty card, we hear?

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken version, so the phrase is matched by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: stamping mocha coffees on a card meant only for cappuccinos would defeat its rules

explanation.surface: A café customer wonders how to cheat a loyalty card that only counts cappuccinos.
explanation.walkthrough: A mocha is a chocolate coffee. To 'put the mockers on' something is a British idiom for jinxing or spoiling it.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the mockers on a plan means ruining or thwarting it, which is one way to break it.

clue.text: Refer to old nationalist revolutionary as intellectual

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: to cite is to refer to
O is the abbreviation for old
N is the abbreviation for nationalist

explanation.surface: Someone is told to describe a former revolutionary nationalist as an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' seems to describe the nationalist, but it turns CITE O N round.
explanation.definitionFit: Noetic is a formal adjective for things relating to the mind or intellect.

clue.text: Orwellian language points to climax

blocks.note: the four compass points, north, east, west and south, here in the order N E W S
a peak is a high point or climax

explanation.surface: A critic notes that Orwell's prose builds up towards its climax.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspeak is the controlled, propagandist language invented by George Orwell in the novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Vast ocean liner I damaged in work for armed forces?

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A huge passenger ship is damaged while being used by the military.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by description rather than synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: National service was compulsory military service, a period spent working for the country's armed forces.

clue.text: Fought lewd comic pinching rump

indicators.note: something comic is played for laughs and out of order, so these letters are jumbled
to pinch is to grip between fingers, so one set of letters holds the other

blocks.note: the letters of lewd rearranged
the rest is the remainder, the rump of something

explanation.surface: A smutty comedian scuffled with someone after grabbing their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rump' looks like a body part; here it means the remaining part, as in the Rump Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle is to grapple and struggle, so wrestled is a past tense for fought.

clue.text: Theory about planets' movement in space and time, mostly

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters that follow are shifted about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, not as a deletion signal

explanation.surface: A description of astronomy: a theory explaining how planets move through space and time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' looks like an instruction to drop a letter, but it is fodder, mixed with space and time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ptolemaic system was the ancient Earth-centred model explaining the motions of the planets, so it is a theory about them.

clue.text: Running away from a nonsense Tory racket? Good

blocks.note: taken as written
BS is a slang abbreviation for nonsense
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory
a din is a racket, a loud noise
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone flees a pointless Conservative scam and is glad of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests a swindle to go with Tory; it is noise. Tory is the nickname for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Absconding means leaving secretly to escape, so it fits 'running away from' as a participle phrase.

clue.text: Most keen to have toilets close to bidet

indicators.note: the close of a word is where it ends, so its final letter is taken

blocks.note: potties are children's toilets
the last letter of bidet

explanation.surface: A bathroom fitter wants the toilets placed next to the bidet.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'potty about' something is a British informal way of being very keen on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Potty informally means enthusiastic or crazy about something, so pottiest is the superlative, most keen.

clue.text: Selfishness, say, over one's millions

blocks.note: e.g. means 'for example', which is what 'say' can mean
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
I is the Roman numeral one, and the 's stands for is
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: Greed shown in someone fussing over their fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is preoccupation with oneself and one's own interests, close to selfishness.

clue.text: Where Venetian leader sits naked for another drink

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so the outermost letters of the phrase are removed

blocks.note: the doge was the elected ruler of Venice, whose seat would be his chair

explanation.surface: A cheeky image of a nude Venetian ruler in his seat, wanting another round.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping the C and E from the outside leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hair of the dog is an idiom for a further alcoholic drink taken to ease a hangover.

clue.text: Eccentric has let in German overdoing the family photos on social media

definitions.text: overdoing the family photos on social media

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of has rearranged
to let a property is to rent it out
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: An odd character lets a German in, while someone posts too many family pictures online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let in' looks like a containment instruction, but each word supplies its own piece. The answer is a recent blend of share and parenting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharenting, a blend of share and parenting, is parents posting excessive images of their children online.

clue.text: China caught drone

blocks.note: c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a drone is a low continuous hum

explanation.surface: News that a Chinese surveillance drone has been brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: China is cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang a china is a mate, so it is a synonym for a friend or chum.

clue.text: Assistant follows lead criminal in state capital

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or bent, so these letters are twisted into another order

blocks.note: the letters of lead rearranged
an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A sidekick tails the chief crook in a regional capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' puts the assistant after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital city of the Australian state of South Australia.

clue.text: Briefly assist veteran stalked by two Celts in central Europe

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: help is to assist, shortened by its final letter
vet is the short form of veteran
II is the Roman numeral for two

explanation.surface: Briefly helping an old soldier who is being followed by a pair of Celtic men somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two Celts' reads as one phrase, but two belongs to the wordplay and Celts starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Helvetii were a Celtic tribe living in what is now Switzerland in Roman times.

clue.text: Solvers to get biscuits

blocks.note: first meaning: people who crack puzzles or codes
second meaning: thin crisp savoury biscuits eaten with cheese

explanation.surface: A reward of biscuits promised to everyone who solves the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers are people who crack codes or puzzles, and also plain crisp biscuits often served with cheese.

clue.text: Bit of American broadcast overheard

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by ear, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: broadcast means sent out over the air

explanation.surface: A snatch of an American radio programme picked up by eavesdropping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of American' reads like a fragment of a show; it is a small coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cent is a hundredth of a US dollar, a small piece of American money.

clue.text: Whitechapel houses extremely advanced

indicators.note: a building houses what is inside it, so the answer sits within the name

blocks.note: found inside the London district's name

explanation.surface: A claim that an East London district's homes are cutting-edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitechapel is a district of East London; 'houses' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech describes very sophisticated modern technology, so it fits highly developed or extremely advanced.

clue.text: Short pause to rest in outskirts of Rugby, between Warwick and Leicester Unis?

indicators.note: short means lacking its end, so the final letter of that word is removed
the outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters of the town are used
in places one word inside the other letters

blocks.note: an interval is a pause, cut short by its last letter
the first and last letters of Rugby
to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: A traveller breaks a journey at Rugby, a town between the universities of Warwick and Leicester.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby lies geographically between Warwick and Leicester, which is the surface trap; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Intervarsity describes contests or events held between universities, such as a match between Warwick and Leicester.

clue.text: Buff wife punches lover

indicators.note: a punch goes into its target, so one letter is driven inside the other word

blocks.note: a fan is a lover or devotee of something
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A muscular wife assaults her boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buff' reads as muscular; it is the pale brownish colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Fawn is a light yellowish-brown colour, practically the same shade as buff.

clue.text: Unmarried woman and Parisian adjust badly

blocks.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman
et is French for 'and', the word a Parisian would use

explanation.surface: A single woman and a Frenchman make a poor job of tuning something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And Parisian' means the word 'and' in French; the printed 'and' does double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To misset something, such as a dial or a bone, is to set or adjust it wrongly.

clue.text: Perhaps neon light at last regains flickers

indicators.note: at last points to the very end of the preceding word, so its final letter is used
a flickering image jumps around, so these letters are shuffled

blocks.note: the last letter of light
taken as written

explanation.surface: A faulty neon sign finally comes back on and flickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks neon as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is one of the noble gases, chemically unreactive elements also called inert gases.

clue.text: I have to follow spy, in case

blocks.note: an agent is a spy
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A detective resolves to tail a spy, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To follow' puts I'VE after the spy. 'In case' sounds like a precaution; case here is grammatical.
explanation.definitionFit: The agentive is a grammatical case in some languages marking the doer of an action.

clue.text: Kind of shade worn by bishop, possibly

indicators.note: clothing worn by someone wraps round them, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a bishop is one example of a chess piece, or man

explanation.surface: A sort of colour a bishop might wear, like episcopal purple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' looks like it means 'type of'; Kind is the definition. 'Possibly' shows the bishop is just one example of a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means compassionate and showing kindness, so it fits the adjective kind.
